name: Lobule VIIB
synonyms: lobule VIIB with the vermian tuber
summary: Lobule VIIB is the narrow hemispheric lobule between Crus II above and lobule VIIIA below, the gracile lobule, on the inferior surface of the posterior cerebellum, with the vermian tuber and folium as its midline counterparts. It lies at the boundary between the cognitive cerebellum of the ansiform lobules and the second sensorimotor map of lobule VIII, and it contributes to both: its lateral part joins the prefrontal loops for working memory and its medial part receives spinal and pontine sensorimotor input. It is supplied by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery, is involved in PICA infarcts and in the cerebellar cognitive-affective syndrome, and its vermian part belongs to the oculomotor vermis.

anatomy.location: Inferior surface of the posterior lobe between the ansoparamedian fissure (below Crus II) and the prebiventer fissure (above lobule VIIIA), extending from the tuber of the vermis laterally as the gracile lobule to the lateral margin of the hemisphere.

afferents.from: Prefrontal, parietal and sensorimotor cortex via the pontine nuclei

efferents.to: Dentate and interposed nuclei; fastigial nucleus (vermis)
Prefrontal and motor cortex via the thalamus

function: Lobule VIIB receives corticopontine fibers from the prefrontal and parietal cortex laterally and from the sensorimotor cortex medially, and spinocerebellar input to its paravermian part, projecting to the dentate and interposed nuclei; functionally it takes part in verbal and spatial working memory and in the planning of sequential movements, and the vermian folium and tuber (VIIA) with lobule VI form the oculomotor vermis that calibrates saccades through the fastigial nucleus. It is one of the lobules in which the cerebellum's contribution to attention and to the timing of cognitive operations has been mapped, and its involvement in posterior lobe lesions adds executive symptoms to gait and ocular signs.

bestView.label: lobule VIIB between Crus II and lobule VIIIA
gracile lobule on the inferior cerebellar surface

imaging.normalAppearance: A narrow lobule on the inferior cerebellar surface on sagittal images below Crus II and above the biventer lobule; the vermian folium and tuber lie at the same level in the midline.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion of the inferior posterior hemisphere including lobule VIIB with ataxia, vertigo and subtle executive change.
Posterior lobe lesion involving VIIB with Crus I-II producing working memory and executive deficits.
Midline lesion of the folium and tuber with saccadic dysmetria and impaired pursuit; medulloblastoma in children, infarct or demyelination in adults.

lesionEffects.mechanism: Disruption of the prefrontal loops through lateral VIIB
Loss of oculomotor vermis calibration of saccade amplitude
Involvement of the paravermian sensorimotor representation

examination: Finger-nose testing for a paravermian component
pearls: VIIB is the border lobule: cognition laterally, movement medially, eye movements in the midline
Saccadic overshoot with a normal brainstem points to the oculomotor vermis
Posterior lobe strokes deserve a cognitive screen as much as a gait test

pitfalls: In the public edition this lobule is not the non-commercial probabilistic cerebellar atlas but a segmentation of the MNI152NLin2009cAsym template itself, made here with FastSurfer's CerebNet module (Apache-2.0 software; meshes `cerebellar-lobule-viib-fs-l` and `-r`). It is a neural network's reading of one average brain rather than a hand-corrected probabilistic map, so treat the fissure lines as approximate: Dice against the private-edition lobule is 0.75 on the left and 0.77 on the right, while the cerebellar cortex as a whole agrees at 0.93.
